In the 1970s, the Transmission Control Protocol (TCP) was developed as a way to ensure reliable data transmission over the network. However, as the Internet grew and became more widely used, it became clear that TCP needed to be improved to handle the increasing amount of traffic and the changing network conditions.
One of the first major improvements to TCP congestion control was the addition of the Slow Start algorithm in the 1980s. This algorithm was designed to prevent the network from becoming overloaded by allowing the sender to gradually increase the amount of data it sends until it reaches a stable rate. This approach helped to prevent congestion and improve the overall performance of the network.
